posts.text:
HB 649 passed the MD House 100–35. It would let the State Commission on Civil Rights enforce nondiscrimination rules on private schools—even if those rules run counter to a school’s religious teachings. Cato's @ColleenHroncich says supporters of educational freedom must stay vigilant.
ow.ly/IL8U50YC3PY

"Chief Justice Roberts had the line of the morning when he said, ‘It's a new world, but it's the same Constitution.' That really does sum up why the government's policy-based arguments had no bearing on the constitutional question,” says Cato’s @Thomas_A_Berry, commenting on the birthright citizenship SCOTUS case.
Ending or curtailing birthright citizenship would imperil the rights of every natural-born American citizen, regardless of ancestry, says the Cato Institute’s @David_J_Bier.

Justice Barrett highlighted that the Trump administration's rationales for denying birthright citizenship would have also denied it to numerous freed slaves and their children—contradicting the original purpose of the Citizenship Clause. This alone is enough to reject the administration’s claim, says @IlyaSomin. 

Learn more: ow.ly/GePr50YC2Jz

📚 Join Cato University in Phoenix on April 18 for a full day exploring liberty with leading scholars and peers. 

💫 Receive free resources and a $100 travel stipend upon completion. 

❗Space is limited. Apply before the deadline on April 8!

✅ Apply here: ow.ly/kQcV50YyepL

"In this country, states are in charge of running federal elections, and Donald Trump isn't. He keeps trying to usurp this constitutionally acknowledged role in defiance of both the law and the Constitution,” says Walter Olson commenting on the new elections executive order.

The US has taken military action against Iran—but Congress hasn’t declared war.
  
The Founders and the Constitution are clear: war making belongs to Congress, not the executive branch, says Cato’s @katherinet57.
  
In this video, she explains the War Powers Act and why no war should be fought without our consent.

Video
The legal arguments in favor of continuing birthright citizenship are solid; the social case is overwhelming, says Cato’s @AlexNowrasteh, commenting on the SCOTUS birthright citizenship hearing.

Real help for small banks starts with less red tape, not deeper government entanglement. More federal guarantees mean more federal control and regulation. Raising deposit insurance caps will result in more of both, explains Cato’s @norbertjmichel.

ow.ly/6pL250YBSzu

To prevent the next TSA crisis, Congress should privatize security screening at the nation’s airports, says Cato’s @CatoEdwards. Expert security firms would handle screening, while the government focuses on regulatory oversight and intelligence—as in Europe and Canada. 
ow.ly/Yuek50YBTr1

Congress should not treat reconciliation as a vehicle for additional spending. If it proceeds, the process should focus on cutting waste and putting the federal deficit on a more sustainable path.

ow.ly/MYYg50YBRJv

Many on the right see Viktor Orbán’s Hungary as a model. In fact, it is a cautionary tale of unrestrained executive power and crony capitalism, the Cato Institute’s @johanknorberg concludes in his latest analysis.

ow.ly/pT9j50YBS67

Cato scholars contend that the Supreme Court should affirm birthright citizenship. The Fourteenth Amendment is clear.  
  
Cato has filed an amicus brief, explaining how and why President Trump’s executive order contravenes the Fourteenth Amendment. 

ow.ly/qMg150YBStg

The latest elections executive order “represents the Trump administration’s continued disdain for the ‘normal’ way in which large changes are made to public policy—either by states or by Congress,” @stephen_richer comments. 
ow.ly/eyYp50YBRyK

Certificate of Need laws accomplish what they’re designed to do—limit competition. The result is fewer hospitals and worse access to care, especially in rural areas. Reform is long overdue, says Cato’s @sslivinski.
ow.ly/WZ6t50YBveZ

Along California’s state beaches, state and local governments have effectively banned independent surf instructors from earning a living. The outcome of their lawsuits against the government could crack open economic liberty litigation far beyond California’s coastline. 

The new Cato Podcast episode explores why First Amendment may be a sharp tool to defend economic liberty. 

Apple: ow.ly/9fXh50YBvan  
Spotify: ow.ly/P5Oe50YBvao  
Our website: ow.ly/k8xO50YBvap

The SAVE America Act isn’t a silver bullet for Republican electoral success, says Cato’s @stephen_richer. “Issues like gas prices, a potential Iran war, airport security lines, and the cost of living will matter far more in determining control of Congress in November 2026.” 
ow.ly/i63c50YBszE

The Trump administration’s proposed “Golden Dome,” modeled on Israel’s Iron Dome and AMD, rests on a system now showing clear vulnerabilities. The lesson for the US is clear, says Cato’s @GiltnerBen. 

ow.ly/xhai50YBstT

America’s debt problem isn’t a mystery—it’s the result of policies lawmakers refuse to fix, says Cato’s @RominaBoccia. We’re running massive deficits in a strong economy, while the burden shifts to younger Americans and future taxpayers. 

Congress knows the problem. What’s missing is the will to act.

Video
